newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syria urges Arabs to improve their industries.
newsitem.headline: Syria urges Arabs to improve their industries.

text.p: Syria has called on Arab states to review their industrial policies and to set up advanced local industries to reduce their $67 billion a year industrial imports bill.
Mohammed Simak, advisor of Syria's industry minister, told Reuters in an interview Arab states have the human, natural and financial resources to do so.

"The Arab countries have over $700 billion of investment abroad, only $13 billion are invested locally, if Arabs direct part of this huge investment to their states they could make good industries," Simak said.
"The Arab workforce is estimated at 96 million. The figure includes big number of skilled workers in various fields apart from others who currently work aborad," he said.
The Arab world, with a population of 240 million, is a big market whose imports, excluding military needs, amount to over $67 billion, he said.

He added that the Arab world has big natural resources including oil, gas, and other mineral resources in addition to the agricultural products like wheat, cotton, sugar beet and sugar cane which make a good base for industry.
Simak said that Arab states should closely coordinate with each other closely to create integrated industries to avoid duplication.
"Arabs should also form a strong alliance to counter the international economic blocs and alliances which are emerging in the world," Simak said.

He admitted that the Arab industries had faced big problems in the past due to the wrong policies on setting up local industries without the appropriate feasibility studies "because the aim was to set up any kind of local industry to limit dependence on foreign industries."
"Local industries which were not studied well did not meet local market needs and were not qualified to compete with other products," he said.
Simak said Arabs should adopt new industrial policies centring on sectors where Arabs have advantages such as the availability of natural resources, low labour costs and cheap energy.

Arab states should also improve and expand the volume of trade among their states as statistics show that inter-Arab trade did not exceed eight percent in the best years of the Arab states trade with the world.
Arabs should give more attention to scientific research to keep their industries up to international standards.
"Statistics show that there are 312 researchers for each one million people in the Arab world while in Israel there are 4.4 researchers for each 1000 people.

He said Arab states had started to move towards improving cooperation and coordination, adding that "an important meeting would be held in Damascus in June 1998 to discuss how Arab industries should prepare for the 21st century.
A conference grouping all Arab industrial ministers, representatives of the private sector and Arab and international organisations would take part in the meeting.

Simak who is heading a committee set up to prepare for the meeting said the conference would constitue a chance for private investors from the Arab world and abroad to seek investment in the industrial sector in the Arab sates.
